groups.title: Enteric-coated capsule (A33903ACE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for disorder of the exocrine function of the pancreas.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 to 4 capsules (20,000 to 40,000 EP units of fat-digesting activity) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, with a meal and plenty of water, swallowing them without chewing. Do not go above a dose of 15,000 to 20,000 EP units of fat-digesting activity per kg of body weight in 1 day. If it is more convenient, the capsule may be opened and the contents taken, but they must be swallowed without being chewed. Be careful not to breathe in the powder.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had hypersensitivity to beef or pork, or if you have acute pancreatitis or an acute flare of chronic pancreatitis. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have cystic fibrosis, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with folic acid preparations, acarbose or miglitol.

If erythema, sneezing, watering eyes, a skin rash or narrowing of the airways occurs, or uncommonly loss of appetite, dizziness, a balance disorder, rhinitis, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, indigestion (a burning feeling, heartburn), stomatitis, malaise, hives, watering of the eyes, bronchospasm, narrowing of the ileum, narrowing of the colon, intestinal obstruction, or ulceration of the mouth and around the anus (especially in children), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (A19000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (D27000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, C, D, E, B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness (poor sight at night); for poor growth of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for the relief of stiff shoulders and neck, numbness of the hands and feet and cold hands and feet in disorders of the peripheral circulation and at the menopause; and for the relief of angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it. An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis (a generalised inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have Wilson's disease, haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil, soya or peanut. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood, gallbladder disease or liver disease; if you have had gout or kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with cardiac glycosides, an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, loose stools, stomach discomfort, constipation, low blood pressure, flushing of the face, an irregular heartbeat, a skin rash, rash, reddening, loss of appetite, a feeling of abdominal bloating, hives, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, upper abdominal pain, red patches, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced function of the central nervous system, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (384200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, back pain, headache, menstrual pain, the reduction of inflammation and the relief of pain after injury, and fever and pain caused by influenza.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time with water, every 4 to 6 hours, up to a maximum of 6 tablets in 1 day. Do not go above the recommended amount.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal effects such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; if blood clotting must not be interfered with or bleeding must be stopped; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, hives or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you have or have had a myocardial infarction; if you have severe high blood pressure, severe kidney disorder or severe liver disorder; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you are taking another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have cirrhosis of the liver, or liver disorder now or in the past; if you have kidney disorder now or in the past; if you have heart failure or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or have had it.

Do not take it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or with high-dose methotrexate.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, digoxin, phenytoin, baclofen, antihypertensive medicines, diuretics, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, low-dose aspirin, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, oral anticoagulants (such as warfarin) or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

If shock symptoms (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like) occur, or rarely aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, a fall in white cells, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, a fall in platelets or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), or nausea, a feeling of abdominal bloating, stomach pain, heartburn, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, gastritis, excessive hidden bleeding, ulceration of the digestive tract with bleeding, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a photosensitivity reaction, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, angioneurotic oedema, blistering dermatitis, erythema multiforme, a maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, jaundice, a rise in AST, ALT or ALP, an asthma attack, hives, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, acute fluid in the lungs, bronchospasm, visual disturbance, altered taste, or from time to time tinnitus, hearing loss, weak sight, headache, depression, dizziness, insomnia, fear, disturbed consciousness, nerve-related seizures, a fall in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, acute kidney failure, generalised oedema, Kounis syndrome of unknown frequency (cardiovascular symptoms occurring after an allergic or hypersensitivity reaction associated with narrowing of the coronary arteries), swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed or swelling of the hands and feet, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (D67000CCM)

groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had hypersensitivity to aspirin or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (an asthma attack, hives, rhinitis); if the user is a child aged 12 years or under; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer.
Do not use it in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, on wounds or inflamed areas, on sensitive skin, on a bleeding skin condition, on infected skin, or on burns.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
This medicine is for external use only; it must not be swallowed.
Be careful that it does not get into the eyes, and if it does, wash it out at once with water.
Do not cover it with an airtight dressing.
When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with medicines that lower blood pressure.

groups.caution:

Do not keep taking it over a long period.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose of this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other oral medicines for rhinitis or with oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines and the like).

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.
